## What changed

**The installer no longer pins an interpreter that root cannot trust.** From a
real install:

```
  в PATH /usr/local/bin/node — v18.17.1; беру /home/user/.nvm/versions/node/v24.20.0/bin/node
  установлено: /usr/local/bin/gitlab-upgrade
  интерпретатор зафиксирован: /home/user/.nvm/versions/node/v24.20.0/bin/node
ошибка: внимание: …/node принадлежит не root (uid 1000)
ошибка:   root будет запускать этот файл — кто может его переписать, получит root
```

The warning was correct and useless. It arrived *after* `установлено`, wearing
the `ошибка:` prefix that every fatal failure in this script uses, and the last
line on screen was a version banner. The person read it as noise and typed the
next command — exactly as designed to fail.

And it is not a passing state. The installer writes the interpreter path into a
wrapper, so root executes a file rewritable by uid 1000 on every run, forever.

So it refuses now, before downloading anything, and names both ways out: install
Node system-wide, or take the risk deliberately with `--node /path`. An
explicitly named path still installs — that is a person who knows the file and
owns the decision — but says so under its own `внимание:` prefix, which no
longer collides with real errors.

Verified by reverting both halves: turning the refusal back into a warning, and
removing the call entirely. Restoring the old ordering was not enough on its
own — the tests now assert that nothing is installed, not merely that something
was printed.

While writing this, the same tests caught that this build container's
system-wide Node was owned by `nobody` — the residue of a `chown` that followed
a symlink earlier in this project. Repaired.
